Propagate margins of error across catchment ACS estimates

Source: R/moe-helpers.R
cacs_propagate_moe.Rd

Computes a margin of error (MOE) for every row of a long-format catchment ACS aggregation. MOE is the half-width of an ACS confidence interval; the U.S. Census Bureau reports it at the 90% level. Each row is dispatched to the MOE formula appropriate for its estimand family (a spatial total, a weighted scalar/proxy mean, or a derived rate), the formula is applied with a confidence multiplier resolved from level, and row-level provenance of the formula used and any fallback is recorded.

Usage

cacs_propagate_moe(data, formula = NULL, level = 0.9, verbose = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

data

A tbl_df or data.table from cacs_intersect_weight() in the canonical long schema, with the per-component aggregation carriers attached as an attribute.

formula

NULL to auto-dispatch a formula from each row's estimand family, a single formula name to broadcast to every row, or a named list keyed by variable that maps individual variables to formula names. The sanctioned formula names are "weighted_sum", "weighted_mean", "proportion_subset", and "general_ratio_conservative".

level

numeric(1) confidence level strictly in (0, 1). Default 0.90, the ACS Bureau convention, for which z = 1.645 exactly.

verbose

logical(1); default TRUE. Emits a single progress-summary condition for orchestrator-level progress capture.

...

Reserved for future extension. The name fallback_chain_max is accepted (with a warning) but has no effect; any other name aborts.

Value

The input data with the moe, moe_formula_effective, moe_fallback, and moe_fallback_reason columns updated, plus a moe_formula_requested column and confidence-level and MOE-provenance attributes attached. When options(cacs.return_se = TRUE) is set, an se column is also returned.

Details

The four supported formula families are documented in detail below.

MOE formula families

Standard errors (SE) and margins of error are interconvertible through the confidence multiplier \(z\): \(M = z \cdot SE\), with \(z = 1.645\) at the default 90% level. Variances accumulate on the SE scale, so each formula divides the component MOEs by \(z\), combines the resulting variances, and multiplies the combined SE back by \(z\).

Family A – spatial total / weighted sum of counts. For a coverage-weighted sum of independent ACS counts, the MOE is the root-sum-square of the weighted component MOEs: $$M = z \sqrt{\sum_j \left(\frac{w_j M_j}{z}\right)^2}$$

Family B – weighted scalar/proxy mean. For a proxy mean built from area- or population-normalized weights (e.g. a median-income proxy), the same root-sum-square form applies with the mean weights, which sum to one and are treated as fixed: $$M = z \sqrt{\sum_j \left(\frac{w_j M_j}{z}\right)^2}$$

Family C1 – proportion subset. When the numerator \(A\) is a true subset of the denominator \(B\), the cross term is subtracted: $$\widehat{Var}(A/B) \approx \frac{Var(A) - (A/B)^2\, Var(B)}{B^2}$$ This expression can go negative; when it does, the row falls back to the Family C2 formula (see below) so a value is still produced.

Family C2 – general ratio (conservative). The default for the package's hard-coded derived rates, used whenever the subset relationship is not guaranteed. The cross term is added, so the variance is always non-negative: $$\widehat{Var}(A/B) \approx \frac{Var(A) + (A/B)^2\, Var(B)}{B^2}$$

C1 to C2 fallback. The fallback is never silent. When a Family C1 row yields a negative subset variance, the MOE is recomputed with the Family C2 formula and the override is recorded per row: moe_formula_effective becomes "general_ratio_conservative", moe_fallback is set to TRUE, and moe_fallback_reason is set to "negative_variance". A zero denominator or a missing input MOE instead yields NA with moe_fallback_reason of "zero_denominator" or "missing_moe". Rows computed without fallback carry moe_fallback = FALSE and moe_fallback_reason = "n/a". A single summary warning reports the fallback counts at the end of the run.

The formula applied to each row can be overridden through the formula argument, and the confidence multiplier through level.

See also

cacs_run(), cacs_derive_rates(), cacs_se_to_moe(), cacs_moe_to_se().

Other core pipeline: cacs_acs_prefetch(), cacs_derive_rates(), cacs_intersect_weight(), cacs_isochrone(), cacs_run()

Examples

# \donttest{
iso <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "legacy_2025_isochrones.rds",
                           package = "catchmentACS"))
acs <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "sample_alabama_subset.rds",
                           package = "catchmentACS"))
iso_subset <- iso[iso$site_id == "AL_SITE_01" &
                  iso$drive_time_min == 5, ]
agg <- cacs_intersect_weight(iso_sf = iso_subset, acs_sf = acs,
                             weight_method = "area", verbose = FALSE)
prop <- cacs_propagate_moe(agg, verbose = FALSE)
head(prop[, c("variable", "estimate", "moe", "moe_formula_effective")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   variable   estimate   moe moe_formula_effective
#>   <chr>         <dbl> <dbl> <chr>                
#> 1 B01003_001    3821.  400. weighted_sum         
#> 2 B11001_001    1450.  263. weighted_sum         
#> 3 B17001_001    3130.  243. weighted_sum         
#> 4 B17001_002    1180.  145. weighted_sum         
#> 5 B19013_001   41490  4955  weighted_mean        
#> 6 B19056_001    1625.  341. weighted_sum         
# }
